title: AgentKnowledgeDump
description: Structured knowledge dump written by an agent before context handoff or compaction. Posted to Port Daddy as a note of type 'knowledge_dump'.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema for forward-compat.

session_id.description: Port Daddy session ID of the dumping agent.

current_task.description: One-sentence description of what this agent is doing right now.

completed.description: Task IDs or short descriptions of completed work.

in_progress.description: Tasks started but not finished. Most important to hand off.

remaining.description: Known future tasks not yet started.

open_questions.description: Questions this agent could not answer and the next agent should investigate.

key_decisions.description: Decisions made during this session that are NOT captured in code or commits. The next agent must know these to avoid relitigating them.

files_touched.description: Paths of files modified or created by this agent.

files_read_for_context.description: Files read as background context. Successor agent should re-read these.

semantic_context.description: Free-form: what this agent understands about the codebase, domain, or task that is NOT derivable from reading the files or git log. Write this for a peer engineer joining mid-task.

handoff_instructions.description: Imperative instructions for the next agent. What must it do first? What must it NOT do? What will trip it up?

successor_context_seeds.description: Specific skills, memories, notes, or files the successor agent should load first.

constraints_discovered.description: Constraints discovered during this session that surprised the agent (not in the original spec). The successor must not violate these.

metrics.description: Optional structured metrics for the Port Daddy fleet ledger.

task_state.current_task: Implementing JWT refresh rotation in relay/auth.ts
in_progress: JWT refresh rotation — wrote the token store, need to wire the rotation handler

open_questions: Should refresh tokens be stored in the daemon DB or in CF KV? CF KV is faster but adds a dependency.
The existing session TTL is 4h — is that correct for the relay use case?

key_decisions.decision: Use HMAC-SHA256 for token signing, not RS256
key_decisions.rationale: No key distribution needed for single-node daemon. RS256 adds complexity for no current benefit.

examples.semantic_context: The relay is a Cloudflare Worker that acts as a zero-trust proxy. Authentication is separate from the main daemon's session system — relay sessions are short-lived and tied to a CF KV namespace, not the SQLite DB. The daemon validates relay sessions via a shared HMAC secret injected at Worker deploy time.
examples.handoff_instructions: Resume from relay/auth.ts line ~180 where rotateRefreshToken() is defined but not wired. Wire it into the POST /relay/connect handler in relay/routes.ts. Run `npm test -- relay` and fix any failures before moving to rate limiting.
constraints_discovered: CF KV has 512 byte value limit in the free tier — don't store full JWT payloads there, store only token IDs.
The relay Worker must stay under 1MB compressed — don't add crypto libraries.
